claim: US$49,528.00, the deficit owing on the defendant's account when it was liquidated by the plaintiff on the 10th December, 1980
requested_remedy: US$49,528.00, the deficit owing on the defendant's account when it was liquidated by the plaintiff on the 10th December, 1980
parties: Plaintiff: Merrill Lynch Pierce Fenner & Smith Inc.

facts.F1: The plaintiff sued the defendant for an amount of US$49,528.00, resulting from a deficit on the defendant's account when it was liquidated on 10th December 1980.
facts.F2: The defendant failed to meet calls made upon him for additional margins, leading to the liquidation of the account.
facts.F3: The defendant counterclaimed that the account was liquidated with his acquiescence, if not his direction, on 8th December 1980, and that the liquidation would have produced a credit balance in his favour of US$18,822.00.
facts.F4: The defendant's claim was not in accord with his evidence, which suggested that the plaintiff had actually liquidated his account on 8th December 1980.
facts.F5: Mr. Chan, the account executive, received a Call Reminder on 4th December 1980, stating that the defendant was required to pay US$30,000.00 to cover his margin.
facts.F6: The defendant paid $170,000 by cheque to cover the margin call on 5th December 1980, according to the defendant, but on 6th December 1980, according to Mr. Chan.
facts.F7: Mr. Chan tried to notify the defendant of a further Call Reminder on 8th December 1980, but was unable to get hold of him until after the market had opened.
facts.F8: The defendant's son, Mr. Cheng Yun Chat, was unable to bring a cheque to cover the margin call on 9th December 1980.
facts.F9: The defendant's account was liquidated on 10th December 1980, resulting in a deficit of US$49,528.00.
facts.F10: The defendant's evidence was not convincing and he appeared to be tailoring his evidence to give a more favourable version of the conversation with Mr. Chan.
facts.F11: Mr. Cheng Yun Chat was not an impressive witness and his evidence was not in accord with the evidence of his father.
facts.F12: Mr. Mathew Chan was a most impressive witness and his evidence was detailed and convincing.
